creator: Corey Wilks

framework_cards.name: Fear of Failure
framework_cards.summary: Concern that the person cannot succeed at the thing itself.

framework_cards.name: Fear of Ridicule
framework_cards.summary: Concern about how other people will evaluate the person or their work.

framework_cards.name: Fear of Uncertainty
framework_cards.summary: Continuing to acquire information after enough exists for a reasonable move.

framework_cards.name: Fear of Success
framework_cards.summary: Approaching success creates concern about the identity, responsibilities, or consequences that follow.

adjudications.correction: Qualification concern alone is not Ridicule; I need evidence of anticipated social judgment.
I need to know how reversible and costly the decision is before calling this Uncertainty.
The project-switch pattern is a useful suspicion, not a confident call without the trigger.
Leave this outside the psychological framework on the evidence given.

recommendations.correction: Separate qualification doubt from anticipated audience judgment in the next item.
Add reversibility and cost to the information-budget experiment.
Add a trigger log before recommending a Fear of Success interpretation.
Verify the legal dependency and act on the remaining available work.

rule_updates.before: Qualification concern can support Failure or Ridicule.
rule_updates.correction: Qualification concern alone supports Failure or skill gap; Ridicule requires evidence of anticipated social evaluation.

rule_updates.before: Repeated information seeking can support Fear of Uncertainty.
rule_updates.correction: Require decision reversibility and expected cost before raising confidence in Fear of Uncertainty.

fresh_case.response: I keep asking for one more market interview even though the decision is cheap to reverse and the next step is clear.

counterexample_prompt: Give us one example of a person your framework is commonly applied to incorrectly.
